title: Eval sprint brain dump: lightweight probes & mixed caching ideas
content:
Quick brain dump from the 2-week eval sprint (notes to self). Goal: sketch small, runnable probes that help decide which of these incremental caching/batching/quant ideas are worth scaling into the runtime. Mostly ideas, heuristics, and tiny experiment designs — half-baked and intentionally informal.

Summary takeaways so far:
- Lightweight probes beat large bench suites for signal-to-speed during early sprints: ~200 targeted prompts + curated failure modes gives more actionable signals than running 10 heavy evals.
- KV cache fragmentation is the silent latency killer: collisions + small prefix hits cause tail latency variance that batching masks poorly. Need per-request cache-affinity metric.
- Mixing a tiny local LRU scratch cache with server-side mosaic cache looks promising: local warms reduce network hop for common prefixes and reduce KV fetch QPS.

Open questions to prioritize:
- How to quantify "cache-affinity" for a request in a way that is cheap to compute online? (affinity ~= fraction of tokens retrievable from local prefix vs remote).
- When is a partial local hit helpful vs harmful (i.e., when partial hits cause divergent model behavior because of stale prefixes or mismatched layer norms)?
- Best minimal probe for hallucination introduced by 4-bit quantization in chat chains (not just next-token perplexity).

Mini experiments to run (order = cheap first):
1) 200-prompt targeted probe: 6 categories (long-context retrieval, short-dialog, math/truncation, tool calls, instruction-chaining, slot-filling). For each prompt measure: latency P50/P95, token-issuing pattern, deterministic rerun diffs. Run across: float16 baseline, int8 QK/KV-only, int4 full-quant. Purpose: find hallucination delta + latency delta cheaply.
2) Local scratch vs no-local scratch: simulate 1ms local lookup + 2ms remote fetch. Use synthetic stream of prefixes sampled from production traces (anonymized). Metrics: cost per token, P95 end-to-end, fraction of requests with local hit > 0.1 fraction.
3) Affinity estimator probe: compute cheap n-gram overlap between request prefix and top-K cached prefixes (K=100) using hashed 4-grams. Proxy metric: affinity_score = max Jaccard over K. Compare affinity_score to actual measured local hit fraction.
4) Partial-cache consistency test: serve identical prompt with local cache entries of varying recency vs no-local. Measure generation divergence (token-level edit distance + semantic similarity via small embedding model).

Experiment details / sketches:
- Targeted prompt sets: use existing internal failures list (JIRA-INF-987) + 120 sampled production prompts (anonymized) + 80 synthetic edgecases I write below. Keep each prompt short (<= 600 tokens context) to make the runs cheap.
- Deterministic reruns: run each condition 3x with different RNG seeds to surface stochastic divergence; compute per-prompt variance for key metrics.

Notes on metrics to capture (not exhaustive):
- Latency: client-observed P50/P95, server staging internal breakdown (parsing, KV lookup, model kernel time, postprocessing).
- Cost: tokenized input + output tokens, plus estimated KV fetches (per-request fetches * cost-per-fetch).
- Quality: lexical edit distance across reruns, semantic similarity (MiniT5 encoder embedding cosine), failure label heuristics (hallucination, truncation, repetition). These labels mostly manual for first pass.
- Cache metrics: local_hit_fraction, remote_fetch_qps, cache_eviction_rate, avg_prefix_length_matched.

Concrete prompt ideas (edgecases I want in small probe):
- Long-context retrieval: "Retrieve the third paragraph of the January 2026 factory memo about heat-sink testing." (simulates doc retrieval chaining).
- Stacked tools: prompt that calls a calculator API then conditions on output (tests function-calling + cache staleness).
- Prompt-chaining hallucination: start a chain with ambiguous facts, then ask for verification two steps later.
- Partial overlap: prompt where 40% of tokens are from cached prefix but remainder request contains new contradictory fact.

Sketch for affinity estimator implementation (cheap):
- Preprocess cache prefixes: shingle into hashed 4-grams, store bloom filter or 64-bit minhash sketch.
- For request: compute same sketch, estimate Jaccard/minhash similarity against top-K (K=100 via LSH).
- Affinity score = max similarity. This is O(#shingles + K * sketch-compare) but can be bounded by LSH candidate set. Should be doable on device in <1ms for short prefixes.

Potential pitfalls / things to watch for:
- Minhash vs exact n-gram: minhash false positives can overestimate affinity, leading to reliance on cache that doesn't help. Need to calibrate with ground-truth overlap in initial runs.
- Embedding-based semantic similarity to detect divergence is expensive; use small distil encoder for probes.
- Quantized models sometimes change stop-token behavior; that skews hallucination heuristics. Include auto-detection for truncated outputs.

Operational notes (how to run locally for dev):
- Runner script (pseudo):
  - inputs: prompt_list.json, model_variant_list, local_cache_sim_params.json
  - spawn worker pods with controlled artificial local-cache latency (env override LOCAL_CACHE_MS)
  - collect metrics to JSONL; post-process with small analysis notebook (not included here)
- Quick sanity check: run 10 prompts across 3 variants; visualize P95 and divergence score in a tiny html.

Links / reading that informed choices:
- KV cache heuristics and MoE patching notes (internal link in CONFLUENCE-ENG-1234) — mostly the thought around prefix collisions.
- Practical quantization + evaluation papers (linked arXiv above, plus internal PR).
- Mosaic-cache paper/blog (high-level takeaways in team channel: slack thread #mosaic-cache).

My hypotheses (candidate decisions):
H1: Affinity estimator with local LRU scratch will reduce tail latency by ~15–25% on common interactive workloads with <5% cost increase.
H2: Partial local hits are net-positive for latency but increase hallucination risk in <3% of prompts — tolerable if detected and fallback triggered.
H3: 4-bit QK-only quant for attention weights + FP16 activations preserves majority of generation quality; full int4 causes subtle alignment drifts that show up primarily in multi-step instruction chains.

Next steps (for next 72 hours):
- Finalize the 200 short-prompt probe set (ask Maya for recent anonymized logs sample).
- Spin up the affinity estimator bench (Samir help on LSH impl).
- Run cheap pilot (10 prompts x 3 variants) and post results to /team/eng-applied-ml/quick-results channel.

Unresolved / TODO (notes-to-self):
- Decide threshold for affinity_score to prefer local cache (empirically choose after pilot).
- Add simple detector for quantization-induced stop-token shifts (heuristic: sudden long gap to EOS across reruns).
- Create small dashboard tile in Console that plots local_hit_fraction vs hallucination incidents (low effort and high signal).

Random half-baked idea (for future):
- "Fuzzy stitching": instead of exact KV match on prefix boundary, try soft-attention-weighted stitching that blends cached KV vectors for similar prefixes; hope to make partial hits smoother. Danger: could amplify hallucination. Worth a probe later if affinity estimator looks good.

End of dump. Will refine after pilot.
